claims.text: In tungsten-based alloys, maintaining coherent nanoprecipitates enhances dislocation transmission at high temperatures.
A uniform spatial distribution of nanoprecipitates enhances dynamic recovery at high temperatures.
Nanoprecipitate coherence and uniformity govern high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten-based alloys.
Targeted heat treatments can vary nanoprecipitate coherence and spatial distribution while overall composition and grain structure are held constant.
Temperatures above approximately 800°C are representative of fusion plasma-facing operational environments.
Facilitated dislocation glide and climb activate dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery reduces stress concentrations during high-temperature deformation.
Dynamic recovery enhances energy dissipation during deformation.
Reduced stress concentrations and enhanced energy dissipation improve high-temperature plastic strain capacity.
Reduced stress concentrations and enhanced energy dissipation improve high-temperature toughness.
Samples engineered for greater nanoprecipitate coherence will exhibit increased high-temperature plastic strain capacity relative to a conventional baseline.
Samples engineered for greater nanoprecipitate coherence will exhibit increased high-temperature fracture toughness relative to a conventional baseline.
The engineered samples will exhibit greater dislocation activity than baseline samples during high-temperature testing.
The proposed mechanism applies to as-fabricated or minimally irradiated refractory tungsten-based alloys above approximately 800°C when composition and grain structure are held constant.
